//! Rolify configuration example generated by rolify-cli.
//!
//! This file shows how to configure rolify for your application.
//! Copy this to your config module and adjust as needed.

use rolify_core::config::RolifyConfig;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Builds the default RolifyConfig for this application.
///
/// Generated by `rolify-cli generate --backend {backend} {role_name} {holder_name}`.
/// 
/// The defaults mirror the gem: strict = false, remove_role_if_empty = true,
/// role_table = "{roles_table}", join_table = "{join_table}".
pub fn build_config() -> Result<RolifyConfig, rolify_core::error::RolifyError> {
    RolifyConfig::builder()
        // .strict(true)  // Enable strict mode (exact scope matching)
        // .remove_role_if_empty(true)  // Remove role when last member revoked (default)
        // .role_table("{roles_table}")  // Custom role table name (default: "{roles_table}")
        // .join_table("{join_table}")  // Custom join table name (default: "{join_table}")
        // .before_add(Arc::new(|record| {
        //     // Veto callback: return Err to abort the add
        //     if record.name.as_str() == "root" {
        //         return Err(rolify_core::error::RolifyError::CallbackVeto {
        //             callback: "before_add",
        //             reason: "root role is reserved".into(),
        //         });
        //     }
        //     Ok(())
        // }))
        // .before_remove(Arc::new(|record| {
        //     // Veto callback: return Err to abort the removal
        //     Ok(())
        // }))
        // .after_add(Arc::new(|record| {
        //     // Notification callback: logging, metrics, etc.
        //     tracing::info!("Role added: {}", record.name);
        // }))
        // .after_remove(Arc::new(|record| {
        //     // Notification callback: logging, metrics, etc.
        //     tracing::info!("Role removed: {}", record.name);
        // }))
        .build()
}

/// Example: Strict mode configuration.
///
/// In strict mode, class/instance role queries use exact-scope matching
/// instead of the override ladder (global < class < instance).
pub fn build_strict_config() -> Result<RolifyConfig, rolify_core::error::RolifyError> {
    RolifyConfig::builder()
        .strict(true)
        .build()
}

/// Example: Custom table names configuration.
///
/// Use this when your database schema uses non-default table names.
pub fn build_custom_tables_config(
    role_table: &str,
    join_table: &str,
) -> Result<RolifyConfig, rolify_core::error::RolifyError> {
    RolifyConfig::builder()
        .role_table(role_table)
        .join_table(join_table)
        .build()
}
